note: R15 Fill A: the designed landscape between the places of Stage One, the Flight Line, Genesis Park and the airfield. Copy shown in game (hotspots, signs). No em dashes, no percentages.

features.p: A shaded fountain court on the walk between the Stellar FBO and the Solport Convention Center: palo verde shade, benches round the basin and a stone runnel carrying the water toward the drive.
A weathered steel ring set square to the morning sun. On the equinox the sunrise sits in the middle of it.
Stacked river stone, the oldest trail marker in the desert. Travellers added a stone as they passed.
Seven steel fins tuned to the prevailing southwest wind. They hum softly on a breezy afternoon.
A single dark stone standing against the western range, a pause before the convention campus.
A stone terrace with two viewfinders over Runway 03/21. Field DGL has been flying here since the biplane days.
A giant chess board in the shade by the market. A game is always halfway through; pick a side.
A weathered steel wall with a thin sheet of water running down it into a stone trough. Recirculated, it cools the air by the plaza.
Two regulation pits forty feet apart, a scoreboard and a bench. Ringers count three.
Three holes on a practice green beside The Landing Club. Bring your own putter or borrow one from the rack.
A stone fire pit with chairs all the way round it, lit every evening for the lodge guests and anyone walking by.
Take a book, leave a book. Stocked by the Club Lodges with desert field guides and paperbacks.
One path in and the same path out, laid in fieldstone on decomposed granite. Walk it slowly.
A horizontal sundial set for this latitude. The bronze gnomon points at the celestial pole.
Reclined stone loungers facing the southern sky, with only amber footlights. Far from city light, the sky here is dark enough for the Milky Way.
Three hammocks strung between timber frames under mesquite shade, a short walk from Genesis Creek.
Six desert natives with their stories, along the walk from the creek gate. Read the signs as you go.

trail.p: A desert classic. Its green bark makes food from sunlight even after the leaves drop in drought.
Slow to grow and long to live. The first arm can take seventy years to appear.
Bare canes most of the year. After rain it leafs out in days and tips each cane with red flowers.
Stores water in thick leaves for years, then flowers once on a tall stalk before the rosette dies.
Its roots can reach groundwater fifty metres down. Its sweet pods fed people here for thousands of years.
Pollinated by a single kind of moth. Fibres from its leaves were woven into sandals and rope.

lookout: A long runway. Face the field and watch the arrivals line up over the western range.
stargaze: The Milky Way core rises over the mountains in summer. Let your eyes adjust for twenty minutes.
sundial: Read the shadow of the gnomon. Sun time and clock time drift apart through the year, so check it against your watch.
